speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and did it follow any specific injury or insect bite?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the moment of injury, and are you currently able to fully extend or bend your finger?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: That inability to flex the distal joint with the finger staying extended is a classic sign of a specific tendon injury. Can you confirm if you have pain or swelling specifically at the tip of your finger, and have you noticed any bleeding under the fingernail?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do you recall if the tip of your finger was forcibly extended during the injury, and is there any numbness in the fingertip?

text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray rules out a fracture, but the mechanism and inability to flex the tip strongly suggest a tendon injury. Can you confirm if you have a small avulsion fracture fragment at the base of the distal phalanx, or is the injury purely soft tissue? Also, does the finger stay straight when you try to make a fist?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the mechanism of forced extension, the inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint, and the absence of fracture, the clinical picture is classic for a rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon, commonly known as a "Jersey finger." DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey finger (flexor digitorum profundus tendon avulsion)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
